statement: A government in a top-3 compute jurisdiction takes equity, a golden share or a formal priority-access security partnership with a top-5 frontier developer (by 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolved: no signed government equity stake in a top-5 frontier developer as of 2026-11-14; equity talks reported in Bloc A; state fund took a voting stake in Bloc B's leading developer (not clearly top-5 globally); defence classified-use agreement signed in Bloc A.

items.summary: Bloc A's defence ministry designated a top-5 frontier developer a 'supply chain risk to national security' after it refused to drop contractual limits on autonomous weapons and domestic mass surveillance; the head of government ordered all federal agencies to stop using its products.
items.detail: Bloc A Defense Secretary Hegseth designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk; President Trump directed agencies to cease using Anthropic. Formally notified 2026-03-05 (NYT). Shows state leverage over frontier developers; reported D.C. Circuit upheld exclusion 2026-09-25 (single secondary source).

items.summary: Hours later, another top-5 frontier developer signed an agreement with Bloc A's defence ministry to deploy its models in classified environments (amended 2026-03-02 after backlash). A deployment contract, not clearly a 'formal priority-access security partnership' under the indicator's wording.
items.detail: OpenAI-Pentagon classified-use agreement 2026-02-27, amended 2026-03-02; reportedly cleared 2026-05-01.

items.summary: The Bloc A head of government said pieces of leading frontier developers 'could be given to the [Bloc A] public'; press confirmed talks with one top-5 developer about a government-linked stake, possibly donated equity to a public wealth fund.
items.detail: CNBC confirmed ongoing talks between Sam Altman and the White House on a possible government stake in OpenAI; Trump named OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI.

items.summary: Bloc B's leading frontier developer closed its first external round (~USD 7.4bn); a state national AI industry fund invested directly and is the only investor holding voting rights and exempt from lock-up. State stake small (~0.3% reported), and the developer is not clearly among the global top-5.
items.detail: DeepSeek Series A >CNY 50bn at >USD 50bn valuation (The Information via Reuters, 2026-06-16); Bloc B's National AI Industry Investment Fund (Big Fund III JV) ~CNY 1bn, direct, voting. Founder Liang Wenfeng ~CNY 20bn.

items.summary: Press reported a top-5 frontier developer proposed donating 5% of its equity (~USD 42.6bn) to the Bloc A government to seed a public wealth fund; not signed, reportedly would need legislation. Another top-5 developer said it was not in equity talks.
items.detail: Financial Times via TechCrunch/TNW 2026-07-02: OpenAI proposed 5% stake; discussed with Trump, Lutnick, Bessent. Anthropic not participating.

items.summary: A top-5 frontier developer committed 5% of its shares to an internal public-benefit fund (pending stockholder approval) rather than to a government vehicle; as of 2026-10-20 the equity-sharing proposals of leading developers remained unresolved.
items.detail: AP 2026-10-20: Anthropic Public Benefit Fund (announced Sunday 2026-10-18); OpenAI Public Wealth Fund idea from April 2026 policy paper. Non-governmental, so not a resolution.

items.summary: Ownership analysis of Bloc B's five leading AI developers: state capital arrives later via funds rather than direct registers (e.g., 18 government bodies reach ~18.1% of one developer by look-through; ~4.9% of a listed developer per its prospectus).
items.detail: WireScreen 'Built and Owned' report: Moonshot 18.1% look-through government; Zhipu (HK-listed 2026-01-08) 4.9% government + 3.5% Tsinghua; DeepSeek 0.28% national AI fund with votes. Publication date approximate (report date not verified).
